# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Notable observations so far:

1. `clientType` in `signInWithProvider` defaults to `'desktop'` on non-web, including iOS/Android now. The comment says "the service keys provider-app allowlists off client_type." The mobile flow uses `fah://oauth/network` redirect — does the server allow that redirect under `client_type=desktop`? The PR description says server now accepts `fah://oauth/network` for `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` — live-verified. But did they verify with `client_type=desktop`? Possibly a mismatch: mobile should probably pass `clientType: 'mobile'`. This is worth flagging as a question/IMPORTANT — the PR says live-verified with client_redirect_uri, but doesn't mention client_type. Since the default stays 'desktop' for mobile, and the service keys allowlists off client_type, there may be a server-side mismatch. But we can't verify server behavior. Worth an IMPORTANT/question-level finding.

2. Android `launchMode="singleTop"` — with AppLinks, when the browser redirects via intent and the activity is singleTop, `onNewIntent` delivers the link; app_links handles that via the activity. singleTop works with app_links (it uses ActivityPluginBinding onNewIntent). OK. But there's a subtle known issue: with singleTop and the browser in front, the intent relaunches... it's fine; app_links recommends singleTop. OK.

3. `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver._listen` — when initialLink matches, it returns early WITHOUT subscribing to the stream. Fine. But the timeout Timer: when initialLink matches, no timer is created — fine since completed.

4. Timer not cancelled on close — same as loopback (timer fires after close, completer already completed or errored; if closed before timeout and never completed, the timer still fires completeError on a completer nobody listens to → unhandled async error? `Completer.completeError` when nobody ever listens to `callback` future... Actually `callback` getter was likely accessed. In the flow, `receiver.callback` is always awaited within try/finally, and even on exception... In NetworkAuthFlow.signIn, if `openUrl` throws, the finally calls `receiver.close()` and `receiver.callback` was never awaited → completer later completes with error → unhandled exception zone warning. But same issue exists in LoopbackOAuthReceiver — pre-existing pattern, consistent. Not new.

5. `_matches` checks `uri.path == '/network'` — but Android manifest uses `pathPrefix="/network"`, iOS has no filtering. A link like `fah://oauth/network/extra` would be routed by the OS on Android (pathPrefix) but ignored by the receiver → hang until timeout. Minor inconsistency, edge case. SUGGESTION.

6. The initial-link race handling: in `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl`, `getInitialLink()` is awaited BEFORE binding the stream listener. Between these, a link could arrive on the stream and be missed — the classic race. Actually they get initial link first, then subscribe. If the link arrives in the gap (delivered to stream, not as initial link), it could be lost. app_links' getInitialLink returns the link that started the app; the stream covers links while running. Gap risk is small but real. Also, on Android with singleTop warm start, a link while the app is running comes through onNewIntent → the stream, not getInitialLink. The race: app paused → browser opens (external app) → link comes back → OS delivers new intent → app resumed with link in onNewIntent. If the AppLinks stream listener wasn't attached yet (because getInitialLink was still awaiting plugin channel), the event might be buffered... app_links streams are typically broadcast; events while no listener are dropped. So the race exists but narrow. SUGGESTION-level robustness: subscribe first, then check initial link — actually the code checks initialLink first and returns early if matching; otherwise subscribes. The reverse order (subscribe, then check initial) would be more robust. Worth a SUGGESTION.

7. Security: deep-link callback carries `code` and `state` in URI — no validation that the callback actually matches pending flow beyond state check in auth_flow (it does check state). OK.

8. `_signInDialog` `_providerSignInSupported => !kIsWeb` — but what about the loopback stub on web throwing? Fine, gate hides buttons.

9. Note the dialog comment says web "the loopback stub throws there" — fine.

10. Test file: uses `throwsA(isA<AuthFlowException>())` with `expect(receiver.callback, ...)` — fine. The timeout test with 20ms — not using fakeAsync; fine.

11. `auth_deep_link_test` close test: `expect(controller.hasListener, isFalse)` — cancel is unawaited; on VM, `subscription.cancel()` on a stream controller subscription removes listener synchronously? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1518
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1518
- **Title**: feat(network): OAuth provider sign-in on iOS/Android via fah:// deep-link callback
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/network-mobile-oauth` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:59:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T02:12:54Z

## PR Description

## Problem
On iOS/Android the network sign-in dialog showed only the developer login — provider buttons were hard-gated off with the comment "the `fa://` redirect is not allowlisted server-side yet".

## Server side (already deployed, NOT this diff)
`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` on ai-native.cloud now accepts `fah://oauth/network` (deploy run success on IstiN/learn.ai@b13b630). Live-verified: `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` with `client_redirect_uri=fah://oauth/network` → 200 (was 400 "not allowed").

## Changes
- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.
- **Android manifest**: `fah://oauth/network` intent-filter (iOS registers the `fah` scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed; the scheme already works end-to-end for OpenRouter OAuth).

## Tests
- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.
- `ui_sign_in_dialog_test.dart`: the iOS test now asserts provider buttons render instead of the mobile note.
- Full network suite: 325/325 green; analyze clean; pre-commit golden gate passed.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place

- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.

While pub get runs, let me check other things:

1. The `clientType` question: `signInWithProvider` defaults `clientType = kIsWeb ? 'web' : 'desktop'` — on mobile it's now 'desktop' with a `fah://` redirect. The comment in the code: "the service keys provider-app allowlists off client_type." The PR description says the server-side allowlist `OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` now accepts `fah://oauth/network` — globally, apparently, not per client_type. Live verification was with client_redirect_uri; presumably with default client_type (desktop). So it probably works. But is `clientType: 'desktop'` semantically right for mobile? It may affect which provider redirect allowlist applies (e.g., Google OAuth app's authorized redirect URIs per client type). If the service keys provider app allowlists off client_type, a mobile flow claiming client_type=desktop might hit a `redirect_uri_mismatch` at the provider. The PR says live-verified the initiate endpoint, but the full browser round-trip on mobile wasn't verifiable in CI. This is a legitimate IMPORTANT-level question but speculative. I'd rate it SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT question. Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" but also not blocking merge... The initiate was verified; full round trip can't be verified from this diff. I'll make it an IMPORTANT question comment on network_session_manager... but wait, that file isn't in the diff! Inline comments must target lines in the diff. network_session_manager.dart isn't changed in this PR. So the clientType concern goes to the general comment, or attach to sign_in_dialog? Better in general comment.

2. Android `launchMode="singleTop"` + deep links: When the browser triggers `fah://oauth/network`, Android launches MainActivity (singleTop) with a new intent delivered via onNewIntent. app_links plugin handles onNewIntent and adds to the stream. OK. But: `android:taskAffinity=""` — fine.

   However there's a real known issue: with `launchMode="singleTop"`, if the app process was killed while the browser was open, the link relaunches the app with a new intent → getInitialLink covers that. OK, handled.

3. `getInitialLink()` called before subscribing to the stream — race window. In app_links, `getInitialLink` reads the initial intent; `uriLinkStream` is a broadcast stream. If a link arrives while `getInitialLink()` is in flight (e.g., user already returning while the async channel call is pending), the stream event fires with no listener and is dropped, and getInitialLink returns null (or the initial link which is null on warm start) → missed callback until timeout. Narrow race but exactly the race the PR claims to handle. SUGGESTION: subscribe to the stream first, then check initialLink, and dedupe (initial link also appears on the stream in some cases? On Android, the initial intent does NOT come through onNewIntent, so no dup; on iOS, the initial link may come through the stream too — app_links docs note getInitialLink and the stream can both deliver. The current code's early-return-when-initial-matches avoids double complete via _completer guard anyway. So reversing the order is safe: subscribe first, then check initialLink; _complete is idempotent.)

   Actually wait — there's a subtlety: if they subscribe first and the matching link arrives on the stream AND initialLink matches, _complete is guarded — fine.

4. `Timer` not cancelled: in DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.close(), the timeout Timer keeps running. If the completer is never completed (flow cancelled before timeout), 3 minutes later completeError fires on a future nobody listens to → unhandled async error in the root zone ("Unhandled exception" printed). Same pre-existing behavior in LoopbackOAuthReceiver. Consistent with existing pattern — SUGGESTION to store the Timer and cancel in close().

5. `_matches` uses exact `uri.path == '/network'` while Android manifest uses `pathPrefix="/network"` — a link `fah://oauth/network/anything` would be routed into the app by the OS but ignored by the receiver → flow hangs until the 3-min timeout instead of completing or failing fast. Minor edge — SUGGESTION.

6. Test gap: `auth_loopback_io.dart` mobile branch (AppLinks wiring, getInitialLink catch) is untested — acceptable since platform channel, but note it.

7. In sign_in_dialog, the doc comment says "Web has no receiver at all — the loopback stub throws there." Accurate.

8. Mobile buttons render, but the dialog can be popped while a flow is in flight? Cancel button disabled while busy. Dialog barrier dismiss? showDialog barrierDismissible default true — tapping outside dismisses the dialog while the sign-in flow runs in background; then when the deep link arrives, callback completes, manager saves wallet... the dialog is gone; that's fine, the sign-in still completes (manager.signInWithProvider completes, updates state). Pre-existing behavior.

9. Check `kIsWeb` import in sign_in_dialog — `package:flutter/foundation.dart` imported, `defaultTargetPlatform` still used elsewhere? The diff removed `defaultTargetPlatform` usage but the import remains — check if `defaultTargetPlatform` is still used in the file... From the full read: line uses `TargetPlatform` nowhere now? Let me grep. In the full file I read, I don't see defaultTargetPlatform anymore. Unused import? `package:flutter/foundation.dart` also provides kIsWeb, so import still needed. Fine.

10. iOS note: PR says "iOS registers the fah scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed". Verified in Info.plist — yes, CFBundleURLSchemes contains fah. But note: on iOS, `fah://oauth/network` with scheme-only registration works.

11. Security review of the deep link: any app could fire an intent with `fah://oauth/network?code=...&state=...` to inject a forged code. But state CSRF check in auth_flow guards it — the attacker would need a valid state. The code is then exchanged server-side; a forged code fails exchange. So no issue beyond the state check which exists. Good.

12. `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.bind` requires `initialLink` — non-nullable parameter but Uri? — fine.

13. The test 'close is idempotent and cancels the subscription' uses a single-subscription controller that never gets a matching event; fine.

14. One more: `_links.where(_matches).listen(_complete)` — errors on the stream (AppLinks stream erroring) are unhandled → unhandled async error. AppLinks stream rarely errors; if it does, completer never completes → timeout covers. OK.

15. Check whether there are CI failures to consider — no ci_failures.md input, so CI status unknown/presumed passing per PR description.

16. ticket ACs: the ticket is the PR description itself. PR satisfies: deep link receiver, gate flip, manifest, tests. 

17. Duplication: DeepLinkOAuthReceiver mirrors LoopbackOAuthReceiver structure (completer, timer, close) — acceptable, similar but distinct receivers.

18. `clientType` default 'desktop' on mobile — worth raising in general comment as a verification item. Actually, let me look at what values the server supports — can't from here. But the sign_in_dialog on mobile now runs `signInWithProvider` with clientType 'desktop'. Since the server keys provider-app allowlists off client_type, and mobile uses a different redirect URI than desktop, there's a real chance the desktop-typed flow with fah:// redirect fails at provider redirect allowlist. PR says live-verified initiate → 200, which was with client_type presumably 'desktop' default... and the allowlist entry that was added is global (`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS`). The full round trip can't be verified here. I'll raise as IMPORTANT question (not blocking, since server change verified initiate; and the PR description explicitly describes live verification).

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1518
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1518
- **Title**: feat(network): OAuth provider sign-in on iOS/Android via fah:// deep-link callback
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/network-mobile-oauth` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:59:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T02:12:54Z

## PR Description

## Problem
On iOS/Android the network sign-in dialog showed only the developer login — provider buttons were hard-gated off with the comment "the `fa://` redirect is not allowlisted server-side yet".

## Server side (already deployed, NOT this diff)
`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` on ai-native.cloud now accepts `fah://oauth/network` (deploy run success on IstiN/learn.ai@b13b630). Live-verified: `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` with `client_redirect_uri=fah://oauth/network` → 200 (was 400 "not allowed").

## Changes
- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.
- **Android manifest**: `fah://oauth/network` intent-filter (iOS registers the `fah` scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed; the scheme already works end-to-end for OpenRouter OAuth).

## Tests
- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.
- `ui_sign_in_dialog_test.dart`: the iOS test now asserts provider buttons render instead of the mobile note.
- Full network suite: 325/325 green; analyze clean; pre-commit golden gate passed.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

Notable observations so far:

1. `clientType` in `signInWithProvider` defaults to `'desktop'` on non-web, including iOS/Android now. The comment says "the service keys provider-app allowlists off client_type." The mobile flow uses `fah://oauth/network` redirect — does the server allow that redirect under `client_type=desktop`? The PR description says server now accepts `fah://oauth/network` for `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` — live-verified. But did they verify with `client_type=desktop`? Possibly a mismatch: mobile should probably pass `clientType: 'mobile'`. This is worth flagging as a question/IMPORTANT — the PR says live-verified with client_redirect_uri, but doesn't mention client_type. Since the default stays 'desktop' for mobile, and the service keys allowlists off client_type, there may be a server-side mismatch. But we can't verify server behavior. Worth an IMPORTANT/question-level finding.

2. Android `launchMode="singleTop"` — with AppLinks, when the browser redirects via intent and the activity is singleTop, `onNewIntent` delivers the link; app_links handles that via the activity. singleTop works with app_links (it uses ActivityPluginBinding onNewIntent). OK. But there's a subtle known issue: with singleTop and the browser in front, the intent relaunches... it's fine; app_links recommends singleTop. OK.

3. `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver._listen` — when initialLink matches, it returns early WITHOUT subscribing to the stream. Fine. But the timeout Timer: when initialLink matches, no timer is created — fine since completed.

4. Timer not cancelled on close — same as loopback (timer fires after close, completer already completed or errored; if closed before timeout and never completed, the timer still fires completeError on a completer nobody listens to → unhandled async error? `Completer.completeError` when nobody ever listens to `callback` future... Actually `callback` getter was likely accessed. In the flow, `receiver.callback` is always awaited within try/finally, and even on exception... In NetworkAuthFlow.signIn, if `openUrl` throws, the finally calls `receiver.close()` and `receiver.callback` was never awaited → completer later completes with error → unhandled exception zone warning. But same issue exists in LoopbackOAuthReceiver — pre-existing pattern, consistent. Not new.

5. `_matches` checks `uri.path == '/network'` — but Android manifest uses `pathPrefix="/network"`, iOS has no filtering. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1518
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1518
- **Title**: feat(network): OAuth provider sign-in on iOS/Android via fah:// deep-link callback
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/network-mobile-oauth` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:59:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T02:12:54Z

## PR Description

## Problem
On iOS/Android the network sign-in dialog showed only the developer login — provider buttons were hard-gated off with the comment "the `fa://` redirect is not allowlisted server-side yet".

## Server side (already deployed, NOT this diff)
`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` on ai-native.cloud now accepts `fah://oauth/network` (deploy run success on IstiN/learn.ai@b13b630). Live-verified: `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` with `client_redirect_uri=fah://oauth/network` → 200 (was 400 "not allowed").

## Changes
- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.
- **Android manifest**: `fah://oauth/network` intent-filter (iOS registers the `fah` scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed; the scheme already works end-to-end for OpenRouter OAuth).

## Tests
- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.
- `ui_sign_in_dialog_test.dart`: the iOS test now asserts provider buttons render instead of the mobile note.
- Full network suite: 325/325 green; analyze clean; pre-commit golden gate passed.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.

- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.

The PR description says the server-side allowlist `OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` now accepts `fah://oauth/network` — globally, apparently, not per client_type. Live verification was with client_redirect_uri; presumably with default client_type (desktop). So it probably works. But is `clientType: 'desktop'` semantically right for mobile? It may affect which provider redirect allowlist applies (e.g., Google OAuth app's authorized redirect URIs per client type). If the service keys provider app allowlists off client_type, a mobile flow claiming client_type=desktop might hit a `redirect_uri_mismatch` at the provider. The PR says live-verified the initiate endpoint, but the full browser round-trip on mobile wasn't verifiable in CI. This is a legitimate IMPORTANT-level question but speculative. I'd rate it SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT question. Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" but also not blocking merge... The initiate was verified; full round trip can't be verified from this diff. I'll make it an IMPORTANT question comment on network_session_manager... but wait, that file isn't in the diff! Inline comments must target lines in the diff. network_session_manager.dart isn't changed in this PR. So the clientType concern goes to the general comment, or attach to sign_in_dialog? Better in general comment.

2. Android `launchMode="singleTop"` + deep links: When the browser triggers `fah://oauth/network`, Android launches MainActivity (singleTop) with a new intent delivered via onNewIntent. app_links plugin handles onNewIntent and adds to the stream. OK. But: `android:taskAffinity=""` — fine.

   However there's a real known issue: with `launchMode="singleTop"`, if the app process was killed while the browser was open, the link relaunches the app with a new intent → getInitialLink covers that. OK, handled.

3. `getInitialLink()` called before subscribing to the stream — race window. In app_links, `getInitialLink` reads the initial intent; `uriLinkStream` is a broadcast stream. If a link arrives while `getInitialLink()` is in flight (e.g., user already returning while the async channel call is pending), the stream event fires with no listener and is dropped, and getInitialLink returns null (or the initial link which is null on warm start) → missed callback until timeout. Narrow race but exactly the race the PR claims to handle. SUGGESTION: subscribe to the stream first, then check initialLink, and dedupe (initial link also appears on the stream in some cases? On Android, the initial intent does NOT come through onNewIntent, so no dup; on iOS, the initial link may come through the stream too — app_links docs note getInitialLink and the stream can both deliver. The current code's early-return-when-initial-matches avoids double complete via _completer guard anyway. So reversing the order is safe: subscribe first, then check initialLink; _complete is idempotent.)

   Actually wait — there's a subtlety: if they subscribe first and the matching link arrives on the stream AND initialLink matches, _complete is guarded — fine.

4. `Timer` not cancelled: in DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.close(), the timeout Timer keeps running. If the completer is never completed (flow cancelled before timeout), 3 minutes later completeError fires on a future nobody listens to → unhandled async error in the root zone ("Unhandled exception" printed). Same pre-existing behavior in LoopbackOAuthReceiver. Consistent with existing pattern — SUGGESTION to store the Timer and cancel in close().

5. `_matches` uses exact `uri.path == '/network'` while Android manifest uses `pathPrefix="/network"` — a link `fah://oauth/network/anything` would be routed into the app by the OS but ignored by the receiver → flow hangs until the 3-min timeout instead of completing or failing fast. Minor edge — SUGGESTION.

6. Test gap: `auth_loopback_io.dart` mobile branch (AppLinks wiring, getInitialLink catch) is untested — acceptable since platform channel, but note it.

7. In sign_in_dialog, the doc comment says "Web has no receiver at all — the loopback stub throws there." Accurate.

Dialog barrier dismiss? showDialog barrierDismissible default true — tapping outside dismisses the dialog while the sign-in flow runs in background; then when the deep link arrives, callback completes, manager saves wallet... the dialog is gone; that's fine, the sign-in still completes (manager.signInWithProvider completes, updates state). Pre-existing behavior.

Let me grep. In the full file I read, I don't see defaultTargetPlatform anymore. Unused import? `package:flutter/foundation.dart` also provides kIsWeb, so import still needed. Fine.

10. iOS note: PR says "iOS registers the fah scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed". Verified in Info.plist — yes, CFBundleURLSchemes contains fah. But note: on iOS, `fah://oauth/network` with scheme-only registration works.

11. Security review of the deep link: any app could fire an intent with `fah://oauth/network?code=...&state=...` to inject a forged code. But state CSRF check in auth_flow guards it — the attacker would need a valid state. The code is then exchanged server-side; a forged code fails exchange. So no issue beyond the state check which exists. Good.

12. `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.bind` requires `initialLink` — non-nullable parameter but Uri? — fine.

13. The test 'close is idempotent and cancels the subscription' uses a single-subscription controller that never gets a matching event; fine.

14. One more: `_links.where(_matches).listen(_complete)` — errors on the stream (AppLinks stream erroring) are unhandled → unhandled async error. AppLinks stream rarely errors; if it does, completer never completes → timeout covers. OK.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1518
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1518
- **Title**: feat(network): OAuth provider sign-in on iOS/Android via fah:// deep-link callback
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/network-mobile-oauth` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:59:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T02:12:54Z

## PR Description

## Problem
On iOS/Android the network sign-in dialog showed only the developer login — provider buttons were hard-gated off with the comment "the `fa://` redirect is not allowlisted server-side yet".

## Server side (already deployed, NOT this diff)
`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` on ai-native.cloud now accepts `fah://oauth/network` (deploy run success on IstiN/learn.ai@b13b630). Live-verified: `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` with `client_redirect_uri=fah://oauth/network` → 200 (was 400 "not allowed").

## Changes
- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.
- **Android manifest**: `fah://oauth/network` intent-filter (iOS registers the `fah` scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed; the scheme already works end-to-end for OpenRouter OAuth).

## Tests
- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.
- `ui_sign_in_dialog_test.dart`: the iOS test now asserts provider buttons render instead of the mobile note.
- Full network suite: 325/325 green; analyze clean; pre-commit golden gate passed.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

**Findings:**

1. ⚠️ IMPORTANT — Race window between `getInitialLink()` and stream subscription (auth_loopback_io.dart). The code awaits `getInitialLink()` BEFORE `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.bind` subscribes to `appLinks.uriLinkStream` (actually bind is called after the await, and _listen subscribes). AppLinks' `uriLinkStream` is a broadcast-style stream; a link delivered via `onNewIntent` while `getInitialLink()` is in flight is dropped (no listener yet), and `getInitialLink()` returns null on a warm-resume → the callback is missed and the flow hangs until the 3-minute timeout. Fix: subscribe to the stream first, then check the initial link (the `_complete` guard already dedupes). Line in diff: auth_loopback_io.dart around line 84-97 (the `if (Platform.isIOS...` block). Line numbers: diff shows the new function. Let me get exact line numbers in the new file.

Actually severity: it's the exact race the PR claims to solve ("initial-link race"), but the current ordering still leaves a narrow race. Realistically on a warm start with singleTop, the flow is: user taps provider → initiate → openUrl (browser activity comes to front) → receiver bound before browser opens (startReceiver happens before openUrl in the flow). So the listener is attached while the app is foregrounded behind the browser. When the redirect comes back, onNewIntent fires → stream has listener. The race only matters if the link arrives in the milliseconds between `AppLinks()` creation/getInitialLink await and bind. Narrow but real. I'll rate IMPORTANT... per guidelines "when in doubt, start one level higher". It's a correctness edge that yields a 3-min hang. IMPORTANT.

2. 💡 SUGGESTION — Timeout Timer never cancelled in `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver.close()`; if the flow errors early (e.g., initiate fails before callback awaited), 3 minutes later `completeError` fires on a future with no listener → unhandled async error in the zone. Store the Timer and cancel it in close(). (LoopbackOAuthReceiver has the same pattern — consistent, so SUGGESTION.)

3. 💡 SUGGESTION — `_matches` requires exact `uri.path == '/network'` but the Android intent-filter uses `pathPrefix="/network"`: a link like `fah://oauth/network/extra` is routed into the app by the OS but ignored by the receiver → silent 3-min hang. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1518
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1518
- **Title**: feat(network): OAuth provider sign-in on iOS/Android via fah:// deep-link callback
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `feat/network-mobile-oauth` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +209
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T20:59:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T02:12:54Z

## PR Description

## Problem
On iOS/Android the network sign-in dialog showed only the developer login — provider buttons were hard-gated off with the comment "the `fa://` redirect is not allowlisted server-side yet".

## Server side (already deployed, NOT this diff)
`OAUTH_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS` on ai-native.cloud now accepts `fah://oauth/network` (deploy run success on IstiN/learn.ai@b13b630). Live-verified: `POST /api/oauth-proxy/initiate` with `client_redirect_uri=fah://oauth/network` → 200 (was 400 "not allowed").

## Changes
- **`auth_deep_link.dart`**: `DeepLinkOAuthReceiver` — completes the OAuth flow from the `fah://oauth/network` deep link via AppLinks (stream listener + initial-link race + 3-min timeout), implementing the existing `OAuthCallbackReceiver` contract; pure seam, unit-tested on the VM.
- **`auth_loopback_io.dart`**: `startOAuthCallbackReceiverImpl` picks the deep-link receiver on iOS/Android; desktop keeps the RFC 8252 loopback.
- **`sign_in_dialog.dart`**: the mobile gate flips to `!kIsWeb` — provider buttons render on iOS/Android like desktop.
- **Android manifest**: `fah://oauth/network` intent-filter (iOS registers the `fah` scheme without host/path filtering — no change needed; the scheme already works end-to-end for OpenRouter OAuth).

## Tests
- New `auth_deep_link_test.dart`: 6 cases (redirectUri contract, stream completion, non-matching link filtering, initial-link race, timeout, idempotent close) — all green.
- `ui_sign_in_dialog_test.dart`: the iOS test now asserts provider buttons render instead of the mobile note.
- Full network suite: 325/325 green; analyze clean; pre-commit golden gate passed.
